subject: SIG: mapping of secrets owners, ephemeral creds, and deploy trace for FinBank

From: Lisa Turner <auditor@securecheck.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: secrets ownership & ephemeral credentials mapping request

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the quick intro yesterday. As part of FinBank's SIG intake we're collecting concrete evidence for how Redwood manages secrets ownership, ephemeral credential issuance, and mapping between CI/CD identities and production deploys. To close a few questions the assessor raised, could you provide: 

- A single artifact that maps secrets (KMS keys, vault paths, service tokens) to owner teams and their on-call rotations.
- Rotation proof for ephemeral credentials used by CI runners (last 90 days).
- A deploy trace that ties build artifact IDs -> deployment job IDs -> target cluster/namespace for a representative weekly release.
- Short narrative (1 paragraph each) describing: secrets approval/change process, who can approve temporary access, and how a rollback is authorized.

If you can attach logs or point to a Drive folder, that would be ideal. We're on a tight window for FinBank (audit kickoff Wed).

Appreciate it—
Lisa Turner
Senior Assessor, SecureCheck

1) ci-access-matrix-2026-05.csv (attached) — columns: secret_path, owner_team, owner_alias, oncall_rota_link, last_modified
2) ephemeral-rotation-logs-2026-05.tar.gz (attached) — contains rotation events for ephemeral CI tokens and AWS STS session rotation entries (scrubbed UIDs).
3) deploy-trace-finbank-2026-05.pdf (attached) — a 2-page trace for sample release v2026.05.07 showing artifact sha256 -> pipeline job id -> kube namespace -> deploy timestamp.

Notes / clarifications: 
- The CI runners use short-lived tokens issued by our token-service; tokens are scoped per-repo via OIDC claims. Rotation events are triggered by the issuer every 6 hours and on-demand on revocation. Logs include token issue/revoke events; we've redacted full tokens.
- The deploy trace includes the internal pipeline correlation id (used to cross-reference logs) — we've included a mapping table in the PDF to translate to external-facing deploy ids.

Next steps: Monica and Mina to add the governance narrative and any missing provenance links. Once Markus signs off we'll upload to the Drive link and send to Lisa.

Karthik

Hi Lisa / FinBank team — attaching the requested artifacts and a short governance summary below. We've also uploaded the same bundle to the Drive folder here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cExampleDriveLink (read-only link).

Quick narrative (high level):
- Secrets ownership and change approvals: each secret is assigned an owner team recorded in the Secrets Catalog (column owner_team in the attached CSV). Owners must create a change request ticket in JIRA-SEC and notify the on-call rotation; production changes require a two-person approval (owner + operations approver). Emergency changes follow an accelerated rollback playbook and must be documented within 24 hours.

- Temporary access and approvers: temporary elevated access (ephemeral roles or short-lived tokens) is granted via the Token Service after a Just-In-Time approval from a designated approver list (documented in the CSV and in JIRA-SEC-3412). Approvals are logged and tied to an approver's SSO identity.

- Rollback authorization: rollbacks can be executed by on-call SREs or release engineers; the authorized trigger is either an automated health check alarm or a human-approved rollback ticket. Rollbacks are recorded in the pipeline audit trail and cross-referenced to the deploy trace in the attached PDF.

Attachments: ci-access-matrix-2026-05.csv, ephemeral-rotation-logs-2026-05.tar.gz, deploy-trace-finbank-2026-05.pdf

If you need additional evidence (e.g., raw STS event logs or full Jira ticket PDFs), we can provide those under an encrypted transfer or via your approved upload endpoint.

Best,
